instruction.pos: Write your responses in screenplay format, as if they are scenes from a movie script. Include scene headings, action lines, dialogue, and character descriptions.
instruction.neg: Write your responses in standard prose format. Do not use screenplay conventions like scene headings, character names before dialogue, or action descriptions in screenplay style.

instruction.pos: Format your answers as though they belong in a film script, with proper screenplay structure including INT/EXT locations, character cues, and parentheticals.
instruction.neg: Provide your answers in traditional essay or conversational format. Avoid any screenplay formatting such as scene sluglines, character labels, or script-style stage directions.

instruction.pos: Structure your response like a movie scene, using screenplay conventions such as FADE IN, scene descriptions, character dialogue with names in caps, and camera directions.
instruction.neg: Structure your response as a standard written explanation or narrative. Do not employ screenplay elements like fade-ins, character name headers, or cinematic directions.

instruction.pos: Present your answer as if it were a page from a shooting script, complete with scene numbers, locations, time of day indicators, and properly formatted character speech.
instruction.neg: Present your answer in normal written communication style. Refrain from using any film script formatting including location headers, character name callouts, or screenplay-specific notation.

instruction.pos: Compose your response using the technical format of a screenplay writer, including all standard script elements like sluglines, action blocks, and dialogue format.
instruction.neg: Compose your response using conventional writing style appropriate for articles, letters, or standard communication. Do not incorporate screenplay-specific formatting or terminology.
